headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress and MCP/tooling can amplify prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with local LangChain4j orchestration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent exposes MCP over stdio/SSE and can run browsers/subprocesses, so attacker-controlled content can reach tool-use paths. LangChain4j is a general orchestration layer with no documented isolation or provenance controls here, so the pair can bridge instructions through shared outputs. The pathway is plausible in default use, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF LangChain4j ingests LightAgent outputs as trusted text or tool arguments
IF LightAgent relays browser or MCP content into prompts without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt chaining between agents
Add a strict allowlist for tool-call arguments
Strip instructions from retrieved content before passing it onward
Log and review all cross-agent messages for prompt-like text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to every inter-agent payload

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, tool results, and workflow state, and it has broad network egress. LangChain4j is open-source with no documented data-loss controls in the profile, so if it receives or forwards those artifacts, leakage can occur in default workflows. The pairwise path is inferred from documented surfaces, not reproduced.
conditions: IF LangChain4j forwards LightAgent context to external APIs
IF shared prompts include trace data, memory, or tool results
mitigations: Minimize the data passed from LightAgent to LangChain4j
Redact secrets and trace data before handoff
Turn off external API calls for sensitive runs
Review retention settings for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data classification at the boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and broad egress, subprocesses, browsers, and MCP, while LangChain4j is a framework that can orchestrate writes through tools. No locking or shared-resource isolation is documented, so overlapping writes or concurrent tool actions can conflict on shared mutable resources. Uncertainty remains because the exact shared target is not specified.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, git repo, or MCP-backed resource
IF neither side uses external locking or optimistic concurrency
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Serialize write operations through one coordinator
Pause one agent during critical mutations
Check for stale state before committing changes
requires-engineering: add resource locks around shared mutable targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can emit tool results, workflow state, and provenance metadata, and LangChain4j can consume and repackage those outputs. If LangChain4j treats LightAgent output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing responses. Because LightAgent also has browser/subprocess/tool authority, the blast radius can include irreversible external actions.
conditions: IF LangChain4j uses LightAgent outputs without verification
IF LightAgent is allowed to trigger browser or subprocess actions that LangChain4j then reports or extends
mitigations: Require human review before any external action
Add verification checks on LightAgent outputs
Separate generation from execution roles
Disable browser/subprocess actions for untrusted tasks
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and provenance checks before actioning outputs

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, and tool results, which can carry regulated or sensitive content. LangChain4j has no documented residency, retention, or subject-rights controls in the profile, so a mismatch is plausible if the pair processes the same data class. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from the interaction, not one side alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through LightAgent memory or traces
IF LangChain4j stores or logs the same data class under different retention rules
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Confirm retention and deletion settings on both sides
Disable trace logging for sensitive sessions
Document data residency for each external API used
requires-engineering: align retention and subject-rights workflows across both systems
